name: Bullet

team.summary: Adi and Alex, YC S26 founders fresh out of AppLovin and Citadel, built Bullet after six pivots.

product.summary: Bullet is a faster coding agent and harness featuring model routing, targeted search, context hygiene, and parallel tool execution.

market.summary: Software engineers and developers experiencing latency with existing coding agents like Claude Code and Codex.

risks.risk: Proprietary binary-only distribution raises supply chain security and trust concerns among engineers.
Harness features can be easily cloned or replicated via custom prompts and open-source alternatives.
History of frequent pivots makes some users skeptical about long-term commitment.

founder_depth.why: Founders have background at AppLovin and Citadel, show deep domain engagement, and shipped multiple iterations before landing on Bullet.

shipping_evidence.why: Live downloadable desktop app, CLI tool via npm (`@trybullet/cli`), video demo, benchmark results, and regular updates.

demand_signal.why: Solid HN engagement with 121 points and 89 comments, with active users testing and giving feedback, though no named revenue customers yet.

defensibility.why: Commenters point out that it is a wrapper/harness easily replicated with prompts or open source, and lacks open-source transparency.

analysis.thesis_fit_reason: Bullet is an AI dev tool (coding agent harness) built by technical founders for software engineers.
analysis.case_summary: Strong engineering velocity and shipping evidence, offset by low defensibility as an easily cloneable closed-source harness.
would_change_my_mind: Open-sourcing the core harness to build community trust
Demonstrating proprietary moats beyond routing and prompting
Showing sustained commercial traction or paying enterprise users
data_gaps: Exact model provider architecture and API routing mechanics
